title: The earth
hookLine: don't spread corruption on the earth after it's set right (7:56)

lines: THE EARTH, A PLACE OF PRAYER.
A FIELD, AN AIRPORT, A BEACH.
cards: A hadith in al-Bukhari has the Prophet ﷺ say that the whole earth has been made a place of prayer for him, and pure. So a Muslim can pray in a field, an airport corner, a parking lot, a beach.

Any clean patch of ground becomes a masjid for a few minutes. Now think about the plastic bag caught in the hedge, or the bottle in the gutter. If the earth is a mosque, that's litter on the prayer rug.

teach.h: FASAD AND ISLAH: SPOILING, SETTING RIGHT.
teach.b: Surah al-A'raf, verse fifty-six, in Pickthall's translation: "Work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering (thereof)." Pickthall's old English needs unpacking. The Arabic is la tufsidu fil-ard ba'da islahiha.

Fasad is corruption, spoiling, things coming apart. Islah is setting right, putting in good order. So: don't spoil the earth after it has been set right, like something made well and handed over in good condition.
The same verse goes on: call on Him in fear and hope; Allah's mercy is near to those who do good.

teach.h: ON LAND AND SEA, BY PEOPLE'S HANDS.
teach.b: Surah ar-Rum, verse forty-one, describes what happens when the warning is ignored: corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned.
Some readers today hear pollution there; classical commentators read it as drought, loss and disorder following wrongdoing. Both hear the same link: what people do shows up in the land.
The hadith fill in the everyday side. In al-Bukhari, if a Muslim plants a tree or sows a field, and a bird, a person or an animal eats from it, it counts as charity.
In a report in Musnad Ahmad, if the Hour comes while you're holding a seedling, plant it anyway.

teach.h: CLEAR THE ROAD: A BRANCH OF FAITH.
teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, removing something harmful from the road is one of the branches of faith. Put those together and the earth isn't scenery.
It's a place of prayer, a trust set in order, and a garden you're still allowed to plant.

how: Muslims may pray on any clean ground; Muslim environmental groups and teachers cite 7:56, 30:41 and hadith on planting trees and clearing the road as the basis for caring for the environment.

o: a trial to be escaped as soon as possible
the property of whoever works the land
a place of prayer, set right, not to be spoiled

s: Muslims may pray only inside a mosque
a hadith says the whole earth has been made a place of prayer, and pure.
a report says to plant a seedling even if the Hour comes
classical commentators read 30:41 as being about plastic pollution
they read drought, loss and disorder; some readers today also hear pollution in it.

games.q: the Hour has come, and you're holding a seedling. what does the report in Musnad Ahmad say to do?
games.why: plant it. even at the very end, care for the earth is still worth doing.

practice: Picture the ground you'll walk on today, your street, the path to the bus, the parking lot at work, plainly, including whatever's been dropped there.
Choose one spot where you'll pick up a piece or two and put it where it belongs, and if you'd like, say bismillah as you bend down.

wordCard.voice: The earth. Al-ard: a place of prayer, set right and not to be spoiled, where planting a tree and clearing the road are counted as faith. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the earth, the land, the ground.

carryVoice: Your line: don't spoil it. The earth is a place of prayer. Day six hundred eighty-four.
